newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 10/11 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 10/11 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 10/11 percent in early trading on Thursday from 11/12 percent at the opening on the back of sufficient liquidity supply, dealers said.
They said liquidity was sufficient following the central bank's injection of 262 billion rupiah in early trading.
Rupiah liquidity was likely to tighten next week due to the month-end factor and half-year book closing, but for now rupiah supply remained largely sufficient, one local bank dealer said.
The central bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 8.34 percent.
